column4: Release-grid helper now has directed wrap, overrun and invalid-period acceptance tests. Absolute kernel sleep and target timing qualification remain open.
Fixed binary ring now has FIFO, overflow, copy and ISR-mask host acceptance tests; target timing, trace selection policy and WCET remain unqualified.
Boot-static first-failure capture now passes field retention, publication and nested-mask host acceptance tests; reset retention, NMI safety and target fault qualification remain open.
Typed read/write/W1C permissions, alignment failures and no-RMW policies now have host bus-observation tests. BSP ordering, bus faults and target access qualification remain open.

TX now rejects null input, unrepresentable counts, unaligned and overflowing register ranges before MMIO; directed host tests cover bounded writes. RX, interrupts and physical timeout handling remain open.

Queued UART service now has host acceptance for producer copies, admission failure, partial writes, budgets, transport error recovery and ISR rejection. Board ownership and hardware timing remain unqualified.
Directed host acceptance covers embedded-NUL records, nonrecursive format data, invalid modifier rejection and exact-capacity bounds; target stack/timing and all backend qualifications remain open.
Portable DMA staging implementation and host binding-rejection tests now linked. A real FPGA DMA engine, IRQ integration and board fault/timing qualification remain open.
Host tests enforce cache-line capacity, alignment, bus windows, CPU range and channel-metadata isolation; real cache-maintenance and bus-address qualification remain BSP obligations.

Directed host acceptance now checks short/zero receive results, generation identity, output aliasing and single cache completion. Physical DMA quiescence and board cache/IRQ qualification remain open.

Host acceptance covers receive alias/copy rules plus failed stop quarantine, repeated recovery, malformed completion and unpublished failed-launch tickets. Real engine quiescence and target cache/IRQ timing remain unqualified.

Typed static queues now have directed value-copy, wrap, direct handoff, staged sender and timeout-boundary host acceptance. Target interrupt timing and complete release-matrix qualification remain open.
Atomic wait enrollment and staged-value handoff have host acceptance tests; target ISR/preemption ordering and physical latency qualification remain open.

ISR-only queue entry points and boot/context rejection now have directed host acceptance, including full/empty output preservation. A verified board ISR dispatcher remains an explicit qualification gap.
Host acceptance now covers direct handoff, staged values, timeout unlinking, no stale sender data and wrap-safe expiration. Target interrupt entry and physical latency remain unqualified.

Static counting/binary semaphore implementation now has host acceptance for invalid bounds, full-width maxima, overflow conservation, IRQ handoff and timeout recovery. Physical interrupt dispatch and timing remain unqualified.

Static event flags now have directed host acceptance for any/all consumption, coalescing, invalid waits, ISR boundaries and consumer versus broadcast ordering. Hardware ISR/preemption timing remains unqualified.
Static mutex ownership, bounded attachment, foreign unlock and scoped failure now have host acceptance evidence; target latency and board qualification remain open.
Existing transitive-inheritance implementation is linked to host inheritance tests plus donation-before-park and handoff restoration acceptance; target timing remains unqualified.
Deadlock rejection, abandoned owner quarantine and explicit quiescent recovery now have linked host evidence; hardware-device recovery proof remains caller/BSP work.

A new three-peer partial-registry regression exposed capacity-dependent initial tie ordering. Initial cursor now selects slot zero independently of configured capacity; red/green host evidence retained, target fairness timing still unqualified.
